title: A Ky Fan singular-value inequality for concave functions
statement:
Let $A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be given, and let $f:\mathbb{R}_+\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_+$ be a concave function satisfying $f(0)=0$. For $k\in\{1,\ldots,\min\{m,n\}\}$, let $\sigma_i(A)$ and $\sigma_i(B)$ denote the singular values of $A$ and $B$, ordered nonincreasingly. **The concave singular-value conjecture.** For every such $k$, 

$$
\sum_{i=1}^k\bigl|f(\sigma_i(A))-f(\sigma_i(B))\bigr|\leq\sum_{i=1}^k f(\sigma_i(A-B)).
$$

This conjecture proposes a generalization of a perturbation inequality for singular values and would provide further applications to low-rank matrix recovery. Its resolution is not given in the source.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.0377

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2012).
source_name: Man-Chung Yue and Anthony Man-Cho So, “A Perturbation Inequality for the Schatten-p Quasi-Norm and Its Applications to Low-Rank Matrix Recovery”, arXiv:1209.0377 (2014).
